tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
schema.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo (a key also hides the on-screen keyboard); 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus, and 'press_key' and 'text' hide it again); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': absolute path (no ~) to the built .app bundle (e.g. /Users/me/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/MyApp-abc123/Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

key.description: For 'press_key': the key or edit command to press.

count.description: For 'press_key': how many times to press it, 1 to 20 (default 1).

state.description: For 'set_keyboard': 'show' or 'hide' the on-screen keyboard. For 'set_appearance': 'light' or 'dark'.

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

The code is auto-detected: starts with <svg = SVG mode, otherwise HTML mode.

IMPORTANT: Call read_me before your first show_widget call. Do NOT narrate or mention the read_me call to the user — call it silently, then respond as if you went straight to building the visualization.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

title.description: Short snake_case identifier for this visual. Must be specific and disambiguating — if the conversation has multiple visuals, this title alone should tell you which one is being referenced (e.g. 'q4_revenue_by_product_line' not 'chart', 'oauth_login_flow' not 'diagram'). Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

widget_code.description: SVG or HTML code to render. For SVG: raw SVG code starting with <svg> tag, must use CSS variables for colors. Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. Use CSS variables for theming. Keep background transparent and avoid top-level padding. Scripts are supported but execute after streaming completes.

# User arbitrations of the blocking report (verbatim, French)

Arbitrages (rapport bloquant, section 7) :

Q1 : (b). Ajouter à §63 « la destination est utilisable dans l'état d'arrivée ».
Q2 : lecture mixte sur l'état d'arrivée : invariants du noyau sur l'état entier, plus ArenaInv de la nouvelle entrée ; NewArenaBase porte cette lecture.
Q3 : réalisation par des pas du noyau. freeSlot (contrat HandlePool v0.5) marque l'entrée libre et incrémente la génération ; préconditions : droit d'administration, pool vivant, handle valide, aucune feuille de l'entrée à Init (Uninit ou Moved), aucune autorité active dérivée d'une compagne de ce pool sur l'entrée ; aucun effet d'endUse. Deux preuves obligatoires :
  (1) témoin complet depuis l'état initial par des pas autorisés : newPool, allocSlot, resolve Modify, écriture, transfer de la valeur vers un local de même forme, unresolve, freeSlot accepté ;
  (2) la mise à jour des métadonnées (état libre, génération) est réalisable par une écriture autorisée sous le droit d'administration.
Q4 : garantie par pool : réécrire D.2, D.3 et D.4(3) sur les compagnes du pool du slot ; les pools imbriqués restent permis ; I1 et les garanties du noyau restent prouvées sur l'état entier.
Q5 : la validation du handle précède le contrôle du droit : fail dans les deux cas.
Q6 : réécrire §86 s4 : « La réémission ne modifie ni les octets ni l'état d'initialisation. Une lecture reste soumise aux conditions ordinaires du modèle mémoire, notamment Init, aux droits d'accès et à la validité de représentation pour le type demandé. La Spec 4 déterminera les obligations de construction et de typage des valeurs réémises. »
Q7 : restreindre §78.3 aux ancres du sous-arbre strict de internal qui couvrent une feuille du stockage administré ; prouver que la clause découle de §78.2 et de I3 (lecture Q9), et l'équivalence de reset avec sa séquence du noyau dans les deux sens.
Q8 : ajouter à §47 : le graphe de possession des statiques est acyclique.
Q9 et Q26 : « valide » = active. §69.2 : endUse est rejeté si une autorité détenue par place a un descendant actif détenu ailleurs.
Q10 : (a).
Q11 : (a) fail ; (b) reject ; (c) reject ; (d) mark exige AdminRight ; (e) grow suit le détenteur actuel du bloc ; (f) fail avant le contrôle du droit (contrat DS-v2).
Q12 : avec le nouveau freeSlot, un handle d'entrée libre est périmé : fail.
Q13 : §71.2 inchangé ; préciser au §36 que MetaRight vise la création ou le recyclage d'autorités sur un stockage existant, pas la création d'une allocation fraîche par alloc ; la concurrence entre appels relève de la spec 2.
Q14 : « opérations d'accès » = O9–O11 ; le préciser au §59.
Q15 : restreindre §40 aux emplacements racines utilisables, comme §49.7.
Q16 : définir I5 : toute feuille épinglée appartient à un emplacement utilisable.
Q17 : lecture actuelle.
Q18 : région dont toutes les feuilles sont de taille nulle : base et provenance de l'allocation de l'ancre effective, comme la région vide.
Q19 : H31a : le jumeau à plusieurs pas (conjonct 5) est accepté.
Q20 : non bloquants (classés).
Q21 : pour chaque cas dont le verdict attendu change, conserver le verdict historique, sa justification et le nouveau verdict fondé sur la v0.1 (tableau dans la description de PR) :
  - H21, H50, H51 : nouveau verdict = verdict obtenu ;
  - H49 : conservé comme test de régression, verdict = verdict obtenu, blocage résiduel documenté (décision NoLock) ; exception explicite : le reset rejeté de H49 est dispensé de jumeau positif ;
  - H16 classé spec 3 ; W2 et W3 : les variantes deviennent les cas ; MM2-H H01 : la variante devient le jumeau ; H10 : l'accès sort de l'allocation ; W1 : la valeur est retirée avant freeSlot.
Q22 : non bloquants (frontières ouvertes de la spec) ; exitRoots retenu comme réalisation de référence.
Q23 : lectures dont un témoin du rapport change un verdict :
  - B#1, B#15, B#33, SP-A4, machine S1 et S2 : lectures actuelles conservées (B#15 imposée par Q9) ;
  - B#28 : remplacée par Q9 ;
  - B#45 : remplacée : chaque pin crée une obligation d'épinglage d'identité fraîche ; une feuille est épinglée tant qu'une obligation active la couvre ; unpin désigne une obligation et ne lève qu'elle ; K.ExternalDone porte sur cette obligation ;
  - H-R5 : sans objet ; DS-R1 à DS-R13 : tranchées par Q11, Q27 et Q28.
  Les lectures sans témoin de différence sont conservées.
Q24 : le fournisseur doit être un emplacement utilisable (§71.2).
Q25 : (b).
Q27 : (a).
Q28 : (c) fail (une pile morte invalide ses marques).

Spec : ne pas modifier `specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.md`. Créer `specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.1.md` à partir de la v0, avec les amendements Q1, Q2, Q6, Q7, Q8, Q9/Q26, Q13, Q14, Q15, Q16, Q18, Q24 et B#45 (§74, §75), en anglais ; en-tête : « Edition v0.1 — corrective candidate, not yet validated », suivi de la liste des clauses modifiées. Commit séparé `docs(specs): add memory model v0.1 corrective candidate`. La reconstruction suit la v0.1.
Contrats locaux : HandlePool v0.5 (Q3, Q4, Q5, Q12) et DS-v2 (Q11, Q27, Q28), changements listés dans la description de PR.
Preuves : refaire celles qui sont touchées ; les garanties de Q1, Q3, Q7 et B#45 sont démontrées sur les états atteignables du contrat, sans hypothèse supplémentaire non normative ; tout échec de preuve est rapporté, jamais contourné. Ouvrir la PR si la condition du brief est remplie.

## Follow-up answers (verbatim, French)

Q9 (suite) : règle unifiée. endUse et free sont rejetés si une autorité qu'ils désactivent — détenue par un emplacement qui meurt, stockage possédé transitivement compris, ou racine d'un stockage libéré — a un descendant actif, quelle que soit son empreinte, que le même pas ne désactive pas. Les cas (1) et (2) sont donc rejetés. La sortie de cadre garde son ré-ancrage, et rejette si aucune origine survivante n'existe (inchangé). I2 au sens « origine active » tient après chaque pas.

Q3 (suite) : remplace Q17. Dans §63.4, §69.2 et §70.3, sont exemptées des contrôles « autorité dérivée active couvrant depuis l'extérieur » les autorités par lesquelles le pas exerce son droit Modify : l'autorité exerçable qui fonde le droit et sa chaîne d'origines (pour le pool : entrée, compagne, internal et ses origines). Les autres autorités actives restent contrôlées. Le témoin Q3 (1) devient : resolve Modify, écriture, transfer de l'entrée vers un local, unresolve, freeSlot accepté, y compris avec internal dérivé. W1 suit le même chemin. Réévaluer W2 sous cette lecture. Ajouter §63.4, §69.2 et §70.3 aux amendements de la v0.1.

(Cases (1) and (2) above refer to: (1) endUse(p) where p owns an allocation q holding a stored authority a, the frame holding b derived from a over another static; (2) free(p) with an empty-footprint derivative of p's root held by the frame.)

# Readings — datastack (DS-v1, non-normative; spec v0 §36, §38, §46, §47, §56, §58, Part XIV, §82)

Module: `formal/Ern/Lib/DataStack.lean` (namespace `Ern.Lib.DataStack`).
Machine-checked examples: section `Witness` of that module (`run_ok`, `reading_above`,
`reading_order`, `reading_mark`, `reading_grow_dst`, `reading_newStack`, `reading_rewind_right`,
all by `decide` on library-reachable states under `Access.Examples.K0`). Four scratch files outside
the repository, re-elaborated against `b4a5cd3`: `../final5/nostack.lean` (DS-R3),
`../final5/d17.lean` and `../../records-chk/q28split.lean` (DS-R13), `../../records-chk/okonly.lean`
(R3).

Source of the contract: the brief's obligation 6 (DS-v1). Spec v0 does not define it (Part XIV
preamble: "The contracts of `HandlePool` and `DataStack` belong to their library abstractions and
are not defined here"). Every entry: clause, reading used, alternative, example whose verdict
changes. "[draft]" = the reading of the draft (`formal/derivability_0.1`, `Lib/DataStack.lean`),
used per policy ("use the draft's reading if the draft matches one of the readings").

## Readings that change verdicts

**DS-R1 "a cell above m" [draft].** DS-v1: "rejects if an active authority derived from internal
covers a cell above m". Reading: the cells at positions `[m.top, top)` (`above`), those that
`rewind m` returns. Alternative A: any cell at position `≥ m.top`. Alternative B: the regions issued
after `m`. Example (`Witness.reading_above`, decided): after `rewind ⟨0,1,1⟩` (top 1) and the
program's `release(5)`, `derive(4, [3], Modify)` gives authority 8, active, derived from `internal`
4, on cell 3 (position 1 ≥ `m0.top` = 0, but ≥ current top). `rewind ⟨0,0,0⟩` is `ok` here; under
A it is rejected. Safety is unaffected: the next `push` over cell 3 is rejected by the effective
right (§43, §61.1). Under B, a block grown after `m` from a base below `m` blocks `rewind` on its
lower part too (draft `opsE4`; not re-run here).

**DS-R2 order of the dead/foreign-mark `fail` and of the right of §36 [draft].** §58: "static
preconditions are checked before dynamic availability, according to the operation's contract";
DS-v1 lists "fails on a dead or foreign mark" first and says nothing about §36. Reading: mark
liveness first (`fail`), then `AdminRight` (`reject`). Alternative: §36 first. Example
(`Witness.reading_order` (1)): a callee frame with no right on the stack value rewinds to the
removed mark `⟨0,1,1⟩`: `fail` here, `reject` under the alternative. Consequence: `mark_no_aba`
gives `fail` unconditionally.

**DS-R3 "foreign" mark.** Reading: a mark is live for stack `j` iff `m.stack = j ∧ m ∈ st.marks`
(`LiveMark`); the stack identity is checked explicitly although, under `MarksWF` (proved on every
library-reachable state), membership alone implies it. The explicit identity check changes no verdict
on reachable states.
`rewind` on a stack index that does not exist is `reject` (no stack value) [draft]. This is a reason
to reject that DS-v1 does not list (narrow check ds4-2). Alternative: a mark of a stack that does not
exist is not live, so DS-v1's "fails on a dead or foreign mark" gives `fail`; or DS-v1 is silent.
Example (`../final5/nostack.lean`): on the initial state `d0` (`DReach.init`, no stack),
`rewind(0, ⟨0,0,0⟩)` is `reject` through `RewindStep.noStack` and neither `ok` nor `fail`; `fail` under
the alternative.

**DS-R4 `grow` with `extra = 0` [draft].** DS-v1 says nothing. Reading: `reject` ("grow" means a
larger size). Alternative: an in-place re-issue of the same region. Example
(`Witness.reading_order` (2)): `grow(0, 5, 0)` in `d9` is `reject`, while release, static checks,
in-place check, `split` and `store` of the same region are all `ok` (alternative: `ok`).

**DS-R5 `grow` of a live block that cannot extend in place: `fail`** (libs.md C10; DS-v1 "fail
otherwise"). The draft rejected it. Reading: the in-place check (`InPlace`: the block ends at the top
and `extra` cells follow) is the availability check of the derived issue (§77.4) and gives `fail`.
Example (`Witness.run_ok`): `grow(0, 5, 1)` in `d7`, where block 6 lies above block 5, is `fail`.
A `b` that is no block of the stack (`Stack.block` gives none): DS-v1 says nothing. Reading [draft
`case_grow`]: `reject` (`GrowStep.noBlock`). Alternative: `fail`, by analogy with DS-v1 "rewind m
fails on a dead or foreign mark" (an identifier the stack does not record). Example
(`Ern.Corpus.DataStack.DS03`, conjunct `GrowStep K0 0 6 1 ds03 .reject`, decided): after
`grow(0, 6, 1)` replaced block 6 by block 9 (`ds03.stacks` records the blocks `[⟨0, 3, 9, 5⟩]`
only), `grow(0, 6, 1)` is `reject` here and `fail` under the alternative (the step reaches
`noBlock` and no other rule).

**DS-R6 order inside `grow`.** The derived issue's static checks (`IssueStatic`) cannot be read on
the state before the release of `b` (the destination still holds `b`, §77.2 "holding no active
authority"). Reading: block lookup and `0 < extra` (`reject`); `release(b)` (`reject` if refused);
`IssueStatic` on the released state (`reject`); `InPlace` (`fail`, the state unchanged); `split`;
`store`. Alternative: in-place `fail` before the release. Changes the verdict when `b` cannot be
released and the block is not in place (`reject` here, `fail` under the alternative).

**DS-R7 `push` without room: `fail` [draft].** DS-v1 says only that `push` uses the derived issue.
Reading: the `size` cells at the top must exist (`top + size ≤ |cells|`); otherwise `fail`
(availability, §77.4), checked after `IssueStatic` on the requested cells that exist. Alternative:
"region belongs to the administered storage" (§77.2, static) gives `reject`. Example
(`Witness.reading_order` (3)): `push(0, 3, 4)` on a stack of 2 cells is `fail`.

**DS-R8 `push` static checks are those of the derived issue (`Arena.IssueStatic`, §77.1, §77.2).**
Not the draft's restricted ones: an `Init` destination is not rejected (spec v0 §77.2, O8.2).
`push` of size 0 is accepted (issue of the empty region): the empty block blocks no `rewind`, and
`rewind` forgets it in the metadata while its authority stays active [draft DS-3].

**DS-R9 `newStack` preconditions: §76.5 applies [draft]** (was R5; review round 2, DS-1). DS-v1
says nothing about creation. Reading: those of `newArena` other than its guard
(`Arena.NewArenaBase`: §76.1–§76.3 and §76.5 "All leaves of the arena value holding `internal` are
already `Init`", read for a stack) and `Guard56 (stackInternals :: others)` (§56). Alternative: drop
§76.5 for a stack (DS-v1 does not take over `newArena`). Same choice as H-R8 for pools. Example
(`Witness.reading_newStack`, decided on the initial state of statics `wsu`): leaf 0, `Uninit`, owns
the storage leaf 1 and so holds its root authority 1 (§47); `newStack(1, 1)` is `reject` (only
§76.5 fails: every other field of `NewArenaBase` and the guard hold), `ok` under the alternative.

**DS-R10 `mark` requires no right [draft]** (was R6; review round 2, DS-1). DS-v1 says nothing about
a right for `mark`. Reading: `ok` on an existing stack, `reject` on a missing one; `mark` changes
library metadata only and creates no right (§36 ¶2, §38). Alternative: §36 ¶1, metadata is modified
"to the extent permitted by the applicable rights and contracts", so `mark` needs a right on the
stack value (`AdminRight`, or a valid `writeShared` over it, §68), else `reject`. Example
(`Witness.reading_mark`): in `d13` (a callee frame entered after the rewind), the callee has no
`AdminRight`, no `Observe` right on the stack value 0 and no valid `writeShared` over it through any
authority; `mark(0)` is `ok` (a mark appended), `reject` under the alternative.

**DS-R11 `grow` destination: the recorded `Blk.dst` [draft]** (was R7; review round 2, DS-1). DS-v1
says only "grow is in place only" and "uses the derived issue"; it does not name the destination.
Reading: the destination recorded for the block at `push` (`Blk.dst`), even when the block value has
been transferred since and that place is `Moved`. Alternative: the place that currently holds `b`.
Changes the arrival state. Example (`Witness.reading_grow_dst`): after the first push (block 5
stored at place 4), the program's `transfer(4, 5)` (§63) moves authority 5 to place 5 and makes
place 4 `Moved` (`d14`). `grow(0, 5, 1)` is `ok` and stores the new block authority 6 into place 4,
which becomes `Init` (§65), while place 5 keeps the released authority 5 (`d15`). Under the
alternative, the static checks of the derived issue (`IssueStatic`) and `store(6, 5)` are `ok` on
the same released and split state, and authority 6 is held by place 5.

**DS-R12 reasons for which `rewind` rejects: §36 applies** (B47). DS-v1: "rewind m fails on a
dead or foreign mark, rejects if an active authority derived from internal covers a cell above m,
otherwise returns those cells to available and removes m and every mark above it". It names one
reason to reject. Reading: §36 applies too (normative: `MetaRight` requires `Modify` exercisable on
the stack value; the abstraction adds no rights to the kernel), so `rewind` rejects without
`AdminRight`. On library-reachable states and for an existing stack, this is the only reason outside
DS-v1's list (`rewind_ok_iff`, R3; that `ok` is then the only outcome is stated by `RewindStep.det` since `b2dcaa9`; before, it
follows from `Guarded.det`, R3). A stack index with no stack gives `reject` for another reason
outside the list, `RewindStep.noStack` (DS-R3). Alternative: DS-v1's list is exhaustive, so
`rewind` is `ok` whenever the mark is live and no such authority covers a cell above it. Example (`Witness.reading_rewind_right`,
decided): `d16` is reached by the rewind to `⟨0,1,1⟩`, the program's `release(5)` and a callee frame
with no parameter or local. There, mark `⟨0,0,0⟩` is live for stack 0 and no active authority
derived from `internal` 4 covers cell 2, the cell above it. `rewind ⟨0,0,0⟩` is `reject` here and
`ok` under the alternative. The kernel sequence cannot realize the alternative: `split` of
`internal` also rejects in `d16`, because `internal` is not exercisable at `Modify` (§61.1).
`AdminRight` has two conjuncts. `d16` tests only `MetaRight` (`internal` is active there); the other
conjunct, `internal` active, is DS-R13.

**DS-R13 a live mark of a dead stack** (narrow check ds4-3). DS-v1: "the stack keeps the ordered list
of live marks; rewind m fails on a dead or foreign mark". It does not speak of a dead stack. §46:
"The arena is **live** if `internal` is active", read for a stack by `AdminRight`. Reading:
`reject` (`RewindStep.static`), forced by the §61.1 check of the derived reset; also by the
`Active internal` conjunct of `AdminRight`. Alternative 1: DS-v1's list is exhaustive (the DS-R12
alternative): `ok`. Alternative 2: a mark of a dead stack is a dead mark: `fail` (under the DS-R2 order the mark is
checked first). Example (`../final5/d17.lean`: `d17_facts`, `d17_only_reject`): `d17` is `d11` (the
rewind to `⟨0,1,1⟩` and the program's `release(5)`) followed by the program's `release(4)` of
`internal` 4. Mark `⟨0,0,0⟩` is live for stack 0, no active authority derived from `internal` covers
cell 2, `MetaRight` still holds and `internal` is inactive. `rewind ⟨0,0,0⟩` is `reject` and nothing
else here, `ok` under alternative 1 and `fail` under alternative 2. The kernel sequence cannot
realize alternative 1: in `d17`, `split` of `internal` rejects because `internal` is inactive (§61.1;
`SplitPre.active`, the same test as the first conjunct of `AdminRight`). Without that conjunct the
outcome stays `reject` through `RewindStep.split` (`../../records-chk/q28split.lean`,
`d17_split_rejects`). So whether the liveness of the stack is part of the §36 check does not change
the verdict. The only alternatives that change it are alternative 2 (`fail`) and alternative 1
(`ok`), and alternative 1 is possible only if `rewind` skips the derived reset.

## Readings that change no accepted program (representation)

- **R1 State.** `DState = ⟨kern, stacks, fresh⟩`, separate from `S3` (§38, §46); a stack is its
  registry index, stacks are never removed; `fresh` is a global counter (§9 "a monotonically
  increasing counter is one possible representation"). The arena registry is not in `DState`: the
  guard reads it through the parameter `others` (§56), as `Arena.NewArenaPre` reads stacks through
  its `others`.
- **R2 Available cells** = positions `≥ top` of the ordered cells (`Stack.entry.available =
  cells.drop top`); `push` and `grow` take cells at the top only and `rewind` returns exactly
  `above`, so this is a set of leaves as in §46.
- **R3 `rewind` kernel part [draft]:** the derived reset of Part XIV restricted to `above st m`:
  `split(internal, [above])` then `release` of the new authority. Plus an explicit §36 check
  (`AdminRight`: `internal` active and `MetaRight` on the stack value) before the split, like
  `IssueStatic.live/metaRight`. **Exact outcome** (`rewind_ok_iff`, hypothesis: the state
  invariant `DReach` only, no `KInv`, no I3): for an existing stack, `rewind m` has an `ok` outcome iff `m` is
  live for the stack (DS-v1), `AdminRight` holds (§36), and no active authority derived from
  `internal` covers a cell of `above st m` (DS-v1). The model does not check the DS-v1 condition
  explicitly. It is the effective `Modify` of `internal` that `split` requires (§61.1, effective
  mode of §43; §61.3 follows). No other check of `split` or `release` rejects on such a state:
  - `internal` has own mode `Modify` and covers the cells (`DReach.stackShape`: §76.2 and §76.3 at
    `newStack`, kept by every step since modes and footprints never change, §42);
  - every anchor names an existing authority (`dBound_of_reachable`), so the fresh authority
    anchors no place (§62.3, §62.4).

  That `ok` is then the only outcome is stated by `RewindStep.det` (`b2dcaa9`); it follows from `Guarded.det`
  (scratch proof `../../records-chk/okonly.lean`, `rewind_only_ok`). With that exclusivity, for an
  existing stack, the only rejection outside DS-v1's list is §36 (DS-R12, DS-R13); a missing
  stack gives `reject` through `noStack` (DS-R3). Not proved here: whether the explicit
  §36 check ever rejects when the `split` check of §61.1 (`internal` active and exercisable at
  `Modify`) would accept.
- **R4 "removes m and every mark above it":** "above" = later in the ordered list;
  `marks := takeWhile (· ≠ m)`. Blocks with base `≥ m.top` are forgotten [draft].
- **R5, R6, R7:** moved to DS-R9, DS-R10, DS-R11 above (they change verdicts or arrival states;
  review round 2, DS-1).
- **R8 Library runs:** `DStep.kernel` admits any kernel step of non-administrative code.

71	deriving DecidableEq, Repr
72	
73	/-- State of the stack library (DS-v2, non-normative; §38: administrative states of library
74	abstractions are separate from `S₃`): the kernel state, the stack registry (a stack is identified
75	by its index; stacks are never removed) and the next fresh mark identifier. -/
76	structure DState where
77	  kern : S3
78	  stacks : List Stack
79	  fresh : Nat
80	
81	/-- Initial state (§47: the kernel's initial state; the library registry starts empty; DS-v2,
82	non-normative: no mark identifier given out). -/
83	def DState.init (statics : Statics) : DState := ⟨S3.init statics, [], 0⟩
84	
85	/-- The `n` cells from position `b` of the stack, leaves of the administered storage (§46; DS-v2,
86	non-normative). -/
87	def cellsOf (st : Stack) (b n : Nat) : List Nat := (st.cells.drop b).take n
88	
89	/-- The cells above mark `m` (DS-v2, non-normative, "a cell above m"; reading DS-R1; §46
90	available leaves): the positions from the top of `m` to the current top, those that `rewind m`
91	returns to available. -/
92	def above (st : Stack) (m : Mark) : List Nat := cellsOf st m.top (st.top - m.top)
93	
94	/-- The stack seen as an administration entry (§46, §36; DS-v2, non-normative): storage,
95	`internal`, available cells (positions `≥ top`) and issued blocks. Used for `MetaRight` and the
96	static checks of the derived `issue`, which read only the storage and `internal`. -/
97	def Stack.entry (st : Stack) : ArenaEntry :=
98	  ⟨st.storage, st.internal, st.cells.drop st.top,
99	    st.blocks.map fun x => (cellsOf st x.base x.size, x.auth)⟩
100	
101	/-- The block of the stack whose authority is `b` (§46 issuances; DS-v2, non-normative). -/
102	def Stack.block (st : Stack) (b : Nat) : Option Blk := st.blocks.find? fun y => decide (y.auth = b)
103	
104	/-- A live mark of stack `j` (DS-v2, non-normative: a mark that is neither dead nor foreign; it
105	decides the `fail` case of `rewind`, §58): the stack is live (`internal` is active, §46 read for a
106	stack; DS2-3: a dead stack invalidates its marks), the mark names stack `j` and it belongs to the
107	list of live marks of the stack. -/
108	def LiveMark (s : S3) (j : Nat) (st : Stack) (m : Mark) : Prop :=
109	  s.Active st.internal ∧ m.stack = j ∧ m ∈ st.marks
110	
111	/-- Decidability of `LiveMark` (§58; DS-v2). -/
112	instance (s : S3) (j : Nat) (st : Stack) (m : Mark) : Decidable (LiveMark s j st m) := by
113	  unfold LiveMark; infer_instance
114	
115	/-- The administrative right of §36 for a stack (DS-v2, non-normative, with §36 and §46 read for a
116	stack): the stack is live (`internal` is active) and `MetaRight`, `Modify` exercisable on the stack
117	value, the place holding `internal`. -/
118	def AdminRight (s : S3) (st : Stack) : Prop := s.Active st.internal ∧ MetaRight s st.entry
119	
120	/-- Decidability of `AdminRight` (§36; DS-v2). -/
121	instance (s : S3) (st : Stack) : Decidable (AdminRight s st) := by
122	  unfold AdminRight; infer_instance
123	
124	/-! ## `newStack` and the guard of §56 -/
125	
126	/-- The stack registry as a registry of live administrations (§56; DS-v2, non-normative): the
127	`internal` identities of its live stacks. -/
128	def stackInternals (s : S3) (stacks : List Stack) : List Nat :=
129	  (stacks.filter fun st => decide (s.Active st.internal)).map (·.internal)
130	
131	/-- Preconditions of `newStack(storage, internal)` (DS-v2, non-normative; §56): those of `newArena`
132	other than its guard (`NewArenaBase`, §76.1–§76.3, §76.5 and §76.6 read for a stack), and the guard
133	of §56 over the stack registry and every other registry of live administrations `others`. -/
134	structure NewStackPre (s : S3) (stacks : List Stack) (others : List (List Nat))
135	    (storage internal : Nat) : Prop where
136	  /-- §76.1–§76.3, §76.5, §76.6, read for a stack (DS-v2). -/
137	  base : NewArenaBase s storage internal
138	  /-- §56: no live administration of any registry uses `internal`. -/
139	  guard : Guard56 (stackInternals s stacks :: others) internal
140	
141	/-- Decidability of `NewStackPre` (§56; DS-v2). -/
142	instance (s : S3) (stacks : List Stack) (others : List (List Nat)) (storage internal : Nat) :
143	    Decidable (NewStackPre s stacks others storage internal) :=
144	  decidable_of_iff (NewArenaBase s storage internal ∧
145	    Guard56 (stackInternals s stacks :: others) internal)
146	    ⟨fun ⟨a, b⟩ => ⟨a, b⟩, fun ⟨a, b⟩ => ⟨a, b⟩⟩
147	
148	/-- Effect of `newStack` (DS-v2, non-normative; §36: registration adds no rights): a stack whose
149	cells are the leaves of the storage, top 0, no block, no mark; the kernel state is unchanged. -/
150	def newStackEff (D : DState) (storage internal : Nat) : DState :=
151	  { D with stacks := D.stacks ++ [⟨storage, internal, footprint D.kern.P storage, 0, [], []⟩] }
152	
153	/-- `newStack` as a relation (DS-v2, non-normative; §56, §58): `ok` or `reject`. -/
154	def NewStackStep (others : List (List Nat)) (storage internal : Nat) (D : DState) :
155	    Outcome3 DState → Prop :=
156	  Guarded (NewStackPre D.kern D.stacks others storage internal) (newStackEff D storage internal)
157	
158	/-! ## `push` (DS-v2: the derived `issue`, Part XIV, §77) -/
159	
160	/-- Metadata after `push` (DS-v2, non-normative; as the `ok` effect of §77 on §46 metadata): the
161	cells leave the available part (the top rises by `size`), the block is recorded. -/
162	def pushMeta (st : Stack) (size a dst : Nat) : Stack :=
163	  { st with top := st.top + size, blocks := st.blocks ++ [⟨st.top, size, a, dst⟩] }
164	
165	/-- `push(j, size, dst)` (DS-v2, non-normative: "push uses the derived issue"): the derived `issue`
166	of Part XIV (`Arena.IssueD`) of the `size` cells at the top into `dst`, on the stack seen as an
167	entry: its static checks (`IssueStatic`, §77.1, §77.2, with `MetaRight` of §36), then `fail`, the
168	state unchanged, when fewer than `size` cells are left (availability, §77.4; DS-v2, Q11 (a)),
169	then `split` of `internal` on the cells (O2) and `store` of the block, of fresh identity `|A|`, into
170	`dst` (O8). -/
171	inductive PushStep (k : K) (j size dst : Nat) (D : DState) : Outcome3 DState → Prop where
172	  | noStack : D.stacks[j]? = none → PushStep k j size dst D .reject
173	  | static {st : Stack} : D.stacks[j]? = some st →
174	      ¬ IssueStatic D.kern st.entry (cellsOf st st.top size) dst → PushStep k j size dst D .reject
175	  | fail {st : Stack} : D.stacks[j]? = some st →
176	      IssueStatic D.kern st.entry (cellsOf st st.top size) dst →
177	      ¬ st.top + size ≤ st.cells.length → PushStep k j size dst D .fail
178	  | split {st : Stack} : D.stacks[j]? = some st →
179	      IssueStatic D.kern st.entry (cellsOf st st.top size) dst →
180	      st.top + size ≤ st.cells.length →
181	      SplitStep k st.internal [cellsOf st st.top size] D.kern .reject →
182	      PushStep k j size dst D .reject
183	  | store {st : Stack} {s₁ : S3} : D.stacks[j]? = some st →
184	      IssueStatic D.kern st.entry (cellsOf st st.top size) dst →
185	      st.top + size ≤ st.cells.length →
186	      SplitStep k st.internal [cellsOf st st.top size] D.kern (.ok s₁) →
187	      StoreStep D.kern.A.length dst s₁ .reject → PushStep k j size dst D .reject
188	  | ok {st : Stack} {s₁ s₂ : S3} : D.stacks[j]? = some st →
189	      IssueStatic D.kern st.entry (cellsOf st st.top size) dst →
190	      st.top + size ≤ st.cells.length →
191	      SplitStep k st.internal [cellsOf st st.top size] D.kern (.ok s₁) →
192	      StoreStep D.kern.A.length dst s₁ (.ok s₂) →
193	      PushStep k j size dst D
194	        (.ok ⟨s₂, D.stacks.set j (pushMeta st size D.kern.A.length dst), D.fresh⟩)
195	
196	/-! ## `mark` (DS-v2) -/
197	
198	/-- Metadata after `mark` (DS-v2, non-normative; library metadata, §36, §38): a mark naming stack
199	`j`, with the fresh identifier `fresh` and the current top, is appended to the live marks. -/
200	def markMeta (j : Nat) (st : Stack) (fresh : Nat) : Stack :=
201	  { st with marks := st.marks ++ [⟨j, fresh, st.top⟩] }
202	
203	/-- `mark(j)` (DS-v2, non-normative; §58 outcomes): `reject` on a missing stack; `reject` without
204	the administrative right of §36 (DS2-1); otherwise `ok`, metadata only (no right created, §36), the
205	identifier is fresh. -/
206	inductive MarkStep (j : Nat) (D : DState) : Outcome3 DState → Prop where
207	  | noStack : D.stacks[j]? = none → MarkStep j D .reject
208	  | static {st : Stack} : D.stacks[j]? = some st → ¬ AdminRight D.kern st → MarkStep j D .reject
209	  | ok {st : Stack} : D.stacks[j]? = some st → AdminRight D.kern st →
210	      MarkStep j D (.ok ⟨D.kern, D.stacks.set j (markMeta j st D.fresh), D.fresh + 1⟩)
211	
212	/-- `mark_rejects_without_right` (DS-v2, non-normative, DS2-1: `mark` requires `AdminRight` on the
213	stack, else `reject`; §36, §58): on an existing stack without the administrative right of §36,
214	`mark` has the outcome `reject` and no other. -/
215	theorem mark_rejects_without_right {j : Nat} {D : DState} {st : Stack}
216	    (hst : D.stacks[j]? = some st) (ha : ¬ AdminRight D.kern st) :
217	    MarkStep j D .reject ∧ ∀ o, MarkStep j D o → o = .reject := by
218	  refine ⟨.static hst ha, fun o ho => ?_⟩
219	  cases ho with
220	  | noStack => rfl
221	  | static => rfl
222	  | ok h ha' => rw [hst] at h; cases h; exact absurd ha' ha
223	
224	/-! ## `rewind` (DS-v2) -/
225	
226	/-- Metadata after `rewind m` (DS-v2, non-normative; as the `ok` effect of §78 on §46 metadata):
227	the cells above `m` return to available (the top returns to the top of `m`), the blocks from that
228	top are forgotten, `m` and every later mark are removed. -/
229	def rewindMeta (st : Stack) (m : Mark) : Stack :=
230	  { st with
231	    top := m.top
232	    blocks := st.blocks.filter fun x => decide (x.base < m.top)
233	    marks := st.marks.takeWhile fun x => decide (x ≠ m) }
234	
235	/-- `rewind(j, m)` (DS-v2, non-normative): `reject` on a missing stack; `fail`, the state
236	unchanged, on a dead or foreign mark, a mark of a dead stack included (DS2-3), before the right;
237	`reject` without the administrative right of §36; then the derived `reset` of Part XIV on the cells
238	above `m`: `split` of `internal` on them (O2), which rejects when an active authority derived from
239	`internal` covers one of them (`rewind_rejects_live_above`), and `release` of the derived authority
240	(O3); `ok`: the cells return to available, `m` and the later marks are removed. -/
241	inductive RewindStep (k : K) (j : Nat) (m : Mark) (D : DState) : Outcome3 DState → Prop where
242	  | noStack : D.stacks[j]? = none → RewindStep k j m D .reject
243	  | dead {st : Stack} : D.stacks[j]? = some st → ¬ LiveMark D.kern j st m →
244	      RewindStep k j m D .fail
245	  | static {st : Stack} : D.stacks[j]? = some st → LiveMark D.kern j st m →
246	      ¬ AdminRight D.kern st → RewindStep k j m D .reject
247	  | split {st : Stack} : D.stacks[j]? = some st → LiveMark D.kern j st m → AdminRight D.kern st →
248	      SplitStep k st.internal [above st m] D.kern .reject → RewindStep k j m D .reject
249	  | release {st : Stack} {s₁ : S3} : D.stacks[j]? = some st → LiveMark D.kern j st m →
250	      AdminRight D.kern st → SplitStep k st.internal [above st m] D.kern (.ok s₁) →
251	      ReleaseStep D.kern.A.length s₁ .reject → RewindStep k j m D .reject
252	  | ok {st : Stack} {s₁ s₂ : S3} : D.stacks[j]? = some st → LiveMark D.kern j st m →
253	      AdminRight D.kern st → SplitStep k st.internal [above st m] D.kern (.ok s₁) →
254	      ReleaseStep D.kern.A.length s₁ (.ok s₂) →
255	      RewindStep k j m D (.ok ⟨s₂, D.stacks.set j (rewindMeta st m), D.fresh⟩)
256	
257	/-- `rewind` has one outcome (§58: a guarded transition has one outcome; DS-v2, non-normative):
258	the cases of `RewindStep` exclude each other, and `split` and `release` are deterministic
259	(`Guarded.det`). With `rewind_ok_iff`, an `ok` rewind is never also `reject` or `fail`. -/
260	theorem RewindStep.det {k : K} {j : Nat} {m : Mark} {D : DState} {o₁ o₂ : Outcome3 DState}
261	    (h₁ : RewindStep k j m D o₁) (h₂ : RewindStep k j m D o₂) : o₁ = o₂ := by
262	  cases h₁ with
263	  | noStack h =>
264	    cases h₂ with
265	    | noStack _ => rfl
266	    | dead h' _ => rw [h] at h'; cases h'
267	    | static _ _ _ => rfl
268	    | split _ _ _ _ => rfl
269	    | release _ _ _ _ _ => rfl
270	    | ok h' _ _ _ _ => rw [h] at h'; cases h'
271	  | dead h hl =>
272	    cases h₂ with
273	    | noStack h' => rw [h] at h'; cases h'
274	    | dead _ _ => rfl
275	    | static h' hl' _ => rw [h] at h'; cases h'; exact absurd hl' hl
276	    | split h' hl' _ _ => rw [h] at h'; cases h'; exact absurd hl' hl
277	    | release h' hl' _ _ _ => rw [h] at h'; cases h'; exact absurd hl' hl
278	    | ok h' hl' _ _ _ => rw [h] at h'; cases h'; exact absurd hl' hl
279	  | static h hl ha =>
280	    cases h₂ with
281	    | noStack _ => rfl
282	    | dead h' hl' => rw [h] at h'; cases h'; exact absurd hl hl'
283	    | static _ _ _ => rfl
284	    | split _ _ _ _ => rfl
285	    | release _ _ _ _ _ => rfl
286	    | ok h' _ ha' _ _ => rw [h] at h'; cases h'; exact absurd ha' ha
287	  | split h hl _ hs =>
288	    cases h₂ with
289	    | noStack _ => rfl
290	    | dead h' hl' => rw [h] at h'; cases h'; exact absurd hl hl'
291	    | static _ _ _ => rfl
292	    | split _ _ _ _ => rfl
293	    | release _ _ _ _ _ => rfl
294	    | ok h' _ _ hs' _ => rw [h] at h'; cases h'; cases Guarded.det hs hs'
295	  | release h hl _ hs hr =>
296	    cases h₂ with
297	    | noStack _ => rfl
298	    | dead h' hl' => rw [h] at h'; cases h'; exact absurd hl hl'
299	    | static _ _ _ => rfl
300	    | split _ _ _ _ => rfl
301	    | release _ _ _ _ _ => rfl
302	    | ok h' _ _ hs' hr' =>
303	      rw [h] at h'; cases h'; cases Guarded.det hs hs'; cases Guarded.det hr hr'
304	  | ok h hl ha hs hr =>
305	    cases h₂ with
306	    | noStack h' => rw [h] at h'; cases h'
307	    | dead h' hl' => rw [h] at h'; cases h'; exact absurd hl hl'
308	    | static h' _ ha' => rw [h] at h'; cases h'; exact absurd ha ha'
309	    | split h' _ _ hs' => rw [h] at h'; cases h'; cases Guarded.det hs hs'
310	    | release h' _ _ hs' hr' =>
311	      rw [h] at h'; cases h'; cases Guarded.det hs hs'; cases Guarded.det hr hr'
312	    | ok h' _ _ hs' hr' =>
313	      rw [h] at h'; cases h'; cases Guarded.det hs hs'; cases Guarded.det hr hr'; rfl
314	
315	/-! ## `grow` (DS-v2: in place, the derived `issue`) -/
316	
317	/-- In-place extension (DS-v2, non-normative: "extension into the space directly after the
318	block"; the availability check of the derived `issue`, §77.4): the block ends at the top, and
319	`extra` available cells follow it. -/
320	def InPlace (st : Stack) (x : Blk) (extra : Nat) : Prop :=
321	  x.base + x.size = st.top ∧ st.top + extra ≤ st.cells.length
322	
323	/-- Decidability of `InPlace` (§77.4; DS-v2). -/
324	instance (st : Stack) (x : Blk) (extra : Nat) : Decidable (InPlace st x extra) := by
325	  unfold InPlace; infer_instance
326	
327	/-- The grown block (DS-v2, non-normative: same base, `extra` more cells, new authority `a`,
328	destination `d`, the place that held the authority of the block, DS2-2; an issuance of §46). -/
329	def growBlk (x : Blk) (extra a d : Nat) : Blk := ⟨x.base, x.size + extra, a, d⟩
330	
331	/-- Metadata after `grow` (DS-v2, non-normative; as the `ok` effect of §77 on §46 metadata): the
332	top rises by `extra`; the block is replaced by the grown block. -/
333	def growMeta (st : Stack) (x : Blk) (extra a d : Nat) : Stack :=
334	  { st with
335	    top := st.top + extra
336	    blocks := st.blocks.map fun y => if y.auth = x.auth then growBlk x extra a d else y }
337	
338	/-- The place that holds authority `a`, if a place holds it (§42: holder; DS-v2, non-normative,
339	DS2-2: the destination of `grow` is the place that currently holds the block authority). -/
340	def holderPlace (s : S3) (a : Nat) : Option Nat :=
341	  match s.A[a]? with
342	  | some y => match y.holder with
343	    | .place v => some v
344	    | .frame _ => none
345	  | none => none
346	
347	/-- `grow(j, b, extra)` (DS-v2, non-normative: in place only, using the derived `issue`): `reject`
348	when `b` is not a block of the stack or `extra` is zero; `release` of `b` (O3); then the derived
349	`issue` of Part XIV (`Arena.IssueD`) of the region of the same base and of size `size + extra` into
350	the place `d` that holds `b` when `grow` starts (DS2-2), on the released state: `reject` when no
351	place holds `b` (there is no destination, §77.2; never on library-reachable states,
352	`DReach.grow_holder`), its static checks (`IssueStatic`, §77.1, §77.2), `fail`, the state
353	unchanged, unless the extension is in place (DS-v1 "fail otherwise", availability §77.4), `split`
354	of `internal` (O2) and `store` of the new block into `d` (O8). -/
355	inductive GrowStep (k : K) (j b extra : Nat) (D : DState) : Outcome3 DState → Prop where
356	  | noStack : D.stacks[j]? = none → GrowStep k j b extra D .reject
357	  | noBlock {st : Stack} : D.stacks[j]? = some st → st.block b = none →
358	      GrowStep k j b extra D .reject
359	  | noExtra {st : Stack} {x : Blk} : D.stacks[j]? = some st → st.block b = some x → extra = 0 →
360	      GrowStep k j b extra D .reject
361	  | release {st : Stack} {x : Blk} : D.stacks[j]? = some st → st.block b = some x → 0 < extra →
362	      ReleaseStep b D.kern .reject → GrowStep k j b extra D .reject
363	  | noHolder {st : Stack} {x : Blk} {s₁ : S3} : D.stacks[j]? = some st → st.block b = some x →
364	      0 < extra → ReleaseStep b D.kern (.ok s₁) → holderPlace D.kern b = none →
365	      GrowStep k j b extra D .reject
366	  | static {st : Stack} {x : Blk} {s₁ : S3} {d : Nat} : D.stacks[j]? = some st →
367	      st.block b = some x → 0 < extra → ReleaseStep b D.kern (.ok s₁) →
368	      holderPlace D.kern b = some d →
369	      ¬ IssueStatic s₁ st.entry (cellsOf st x.base (x.size + extra)) d →
370	      GrowStep k j b extra D .reject
371	  | fail {st : Stack} {x : Blk} {s₁ : S3} {d : Nat} : D.stacks[j]? = some st →
372	      st.block b = some x → 0 < extra → ReleaseStep b D.kern (.ok s₁) →
373	      holderPlace D.kern b = some d →
374	      IssueStatic s₁ st.entry (cellsOf st x.base (x.size + extra)) d →
375	      ¬ InPlace st x extra → GrowStep k j b extra D .fail
376	  | split {st : Stack} {x : Blk} {s₁ : S3} {d : Nat} : D.stacks[j]? = some st →
377	      st.block b = some x → 0 < extra → ReleaseStep b D.kern (.ok s₁) →
378	      holderPlace D.kern b = some d →
379	      IssueStatic s₁ st.entry (cellsOf st x.base (x.size + extra)) d → InPlace st x extra →
380	      SplitStep k st.internal [cellsOf st x.base (x.size + extra)] s₁ .reject →
381	      GrowStep k j b extra D .reject
382	  | store {st : Stack} {x : Blk} {s₁ s₂ : S3} {d : Nat} : D.stacks[j]? = some st →
383	      st.block b = some x → 0 < extra → ReleaseStep b D.kern (.ok s₁) →
384	      holderPlace D.kern b = some d →
385	      IssueStatic s₁ st.entry (cellsOf st x.base (x.size + extra)) d → InPlace st x extra →
386	      SplitStep k st.internal [cellsOf st x.base (x.size + extra)] s₁ (.ok s₂) →
387	      StoreStep s₁.A.length d s₂ .reject → GrowStep k j b extra D .reject
388	  | ok {st : Stack} {x : Blk} {s₁ s₂ s₃ : S3} {d : Nat} : D.stacks[j]? = some st →
389	      st.block b = some x → 0 < extra → ReleaseStep b D.kern (.ok s₁) →
390	      holderPlace D.kern b = some d →
391	      IssueStatic s₁ st.entry (cellsOf st x.base (x.size + extra)) d → InPlace st x extra →
392	      SplitStep k st.internal [cellsOf st x.base (x.size + extra)] s₁ (.ok s₂) →
393	      StoreStep s₁.A.length d s₂ (.ok s₃) →
394	      GrowStep k j b extra D
395	        (.ok ⟨s₃, D.stacks.set j (growMeta st x extra s₁.A.length d), D.fresh⟩)
396	
397	/-! ## Library runs (DS-v2; §36, §56, §57) -/
398	
399	/-- One `ok` step of the stack library (DS-v2, non-normative): a kernel step O1–O16 of
400	non-administrative code, the registry unchanged; `newStack` with the guard of §56 against the other
401	registries `others`; `push`, `mark`, `rewind`, `grow`. -/
402	inductive DStep (k : K) : DState → DState → Prop where
403	  | kernel {D : DState} {s' : S3} : KStep k D.kern s' → DStep k D ⟨s', D.stacks, D.fresh⟩
404	  | newStack {D D' : DState} {others : List (List Nat)} {storage i : Nat} :
405	      NewStackStep others storage i D (.ok D') → DStep k D D'
406	  | push {D D' : DState} {j size dst : Nat} : PushStep k j size dst D (.ok D') → DStep k D D'
407	  | mark {D D' : DState} {j : Nat} : MarkStep j D (.ok D') → DStep k D D'
408	  | rewind {D D' : DState} {j : Nat} {m : Mark} : RewindStep k j m D (.ok D') → DStep k D D'
409	  | grow {D D' : DState} {j b extra : Nat} : GrowStep k j b extra D (.ok D') → DStep k D D'
410	
411	/-- States reachable from the initial state by library steps (DS-v2, non-normative; §47). -/
412	inductive DReach (k : K) (statics : Statics) : DState → Prop where
413	  | init : DReach k statics (DState.init statics)
414	  | step {D D' : DState} : DReach k statics D → DStep k D D' → DReach k statics D'
415	
416	/-- Finite sequences of library steps (DS-v2, non-normative; §58 `ok` transitions). -/
417	inductive DRun (k : K) : DState → DState → Prop where
418	  | refl (D : DState) : DRun k D D
419	  | tail {D D' D'' : DState} : DRun k D D' → DStep k D' D'' → DRun k D D''
420	
421	/-- The kernel part of a library step is reached by kernel steps (§36: the abstraction adds no
422	rights to the kernel; Part XIV: `issue` is `split` then `store`, the reset part of `rewind` is
423	`split` then `release`; DS-v2). -/
424	theorem DStep.reachable {k : K} {statics : Statics} {D D' : DState}
425	    (hr : Reachable k statics D.kern) (h : DStep k D D') : Reachable k statics D'.kern := by
426	  cases h with
427	  | kernel hk => exact .step hr hk
428	  | newStack hs => obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 hs; exact hr
429	  | push hs =>
430	    cases hs with
431	    | ok _ _ _ hsp hst => exact .step (.step hr (.split hsp)) (.store hst)
432	  | mark hs => cases hs with | ok _ _ => exact hr
433	  | rewind hs =>
434	    cases hs with
435	    | ok _ _ _ hsp hrl => exact .step (.step hr (.split hsp)) (.release hrl)
436	  | grow hs =>
437	    cases hs with
438	    | ok _ _ _ hrl _ _ _ hsp hst =>
439	      exact .step (.step (.step hr (.release hrl)) (.split hsp)) (.store hst)
440	
441	/-- The kernel state of every library-reachable state is kernel-reachable (§36, §57; DS-v2). -/
442	theorem DReach.reachable {k : K} {statics : Statics} {D : DState} (h : DReach k statics D) :
443	    Reachable k statics D.kern := by
444	  induction h with
445	  | init => exact .init
446	  | step _ hs ih => exact hs.reachable ih
447	
448	/-! ## Helper lemmas (lists, kernel effects) -/
449	
450	/-- Reading a list after `set` (support for the §46 metadata updates of DS-v2). -/
451	theorem getElem?_set_cases {α : Type} {l : List α} {j i : Nat} {v x : α}
452	    (h : (l.set j v)[i]? = some x) : (i = j ∧ x = v) ∨ (i ≠ j ∧ l[i]? = some x) := by
453	  rw [List.getElem?_set] at h
454	  by_cases hij : j = i
455	  · subst hij; simp only [↓reduceIte] at h; split at h
456	    · cases h; exact .inl ⟨rfl, rfl⟩
457	    · cases h
458	  · simp only [hij, ↓reduceIte] at h; exact .inr ⟨Ne.symm hij, h⟩
459	
460	/-- Reading a list after appending one element (support for the §46 metadata updates of
461	DS-v2). -/
462	theorem getElem?_append_single {α : Type} {l : List α} {x y : α} {i : Nat}
463	    (h : (l ++ [x])[i]? = some y) : l[i]? = some y ∨ y = x := by
464	  rw [List.getElem?_append] at h
465	  split at h
466	  · exact .inl h
467	  · cases hc : i - l.length with
468	    | zero => rw [hc] at h; simp at h; exact .inr h.symm
469	    | succ n => rw [hc] at h; simp at h
470	
471	/-- `takeWhile (· ≠ m)` stops at the first occurrence of `m` (support for the §46 metadata of
472	DS-v2 `rewind`). -/
473	theorem takeWhile_ne_append {m : Mark} : ∀ {pre : List Mark} (post : List Mark), m ∉ pre →
474	    (pre ++ m :: post).takeWhile (fun x => decide (x ≠ m)) = pre
475	  | [], post, _ => by simp
476	  | a :: pre, post, h => by
477	    have ha : a ≠ m := fun e => h (e ▸ List.mem_cons_self ..)
478	    have ih := takeWhile_ne_append (pre := pre) post (fun h' => h (List.mem_cons_of_mem _ h'))
479	    rw [List.cons_append, List.takeWhile_cons]
480	    simp only [ha, ne_eq, not_false_eq_true, decide_true, ↓reduceIte, ih]
481	
482	/-- A prefix of `take` (support for DS-v2 `grow`, §46 metadata: the old cells are a prefix of the
483	new ones). -/
484	theorem take_prefix_take_add {α : Type} : ∀ (l : List α) (n e : Nat), l.take n <+: l.take (n + e)
485	  | [], n, e => ⟨[], by rw [List.take_nil, List.take_nil]; rfl⟩
486	  | _ :: _, 0, _ => ⟨_, List.nil_append _⟩
487	  | a :: l, n + 1, e => by
488	    obtain ⟨t, ht⟩ := take_prefix_take_add l n e
489	    exact ⟨t, by rw [Nat.add_right_comm, List.take_succ_cons, List.take_succ_cons,
490	      List.cons_append, ht]⟩
491	
492	/-- The cells of a block are a prefix of the cells of the block grown from the same base (DS-v2,
493	non-normative, "same base"; §46 issued regions). -/
494	theorem cellsOf_prefix (st : Stack) (b n e : Nat) : cellsOf st b n <+: cellsOf st b (n + e) :=
495	  take_prefix_take_add _ _ _
496	
497	/-- `release` keeps the identities of the authorities (§62, `ok` effect; support for DS-v2). -/
498	theorem releaseEff_len (s : S3) (a : Nat) : (releaseEff s a).A.length = s.A.length := by
499	  unfold releaseEff; split <;> simp

1	import Ern.MemoryModel.Arena
2	import Ern.MemoryModel.Refinement
3	
4	/-!
5	# DataStack: a library administrative abstraction (contract DS-v2, non-normative)
6	
7	A `DataStack` instance of `specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.1.md`. The spec does not define
8	its contract (Part XIV preamble: "The contracts of `HandlePool` and `DataStack` belong to their
9	library abstractions and are not defined here"). The contract formalized here is the library
10	contract **DS-v2**, which is **not normative**: every definition below that encodes a DS-v2 item
11	says so. The normative clauses that constrain it are §36 (`MetaRight` requires `Modify` exercisable
12	on the stack value; the abstraction adds no rights to the kernel), §38 and §46 (library state
13	separate from `S₃`), §47 (empty initial registry), §56 (guard over all registries of live
14	administrations) and §58 (outcomes).
15	
16	DS-v2 is DS-v1 with three changes. DS-v1: marks carry the stack identity and a fresh mark
17	identifier; the stack keeps the ordered list of live marks; `rewind m` fails on a dead or foreign
18	mark, rejects if an active authority derived from `internal` covers a cell above `m`, otherwise
19	returns those cells to available and removes `m` and every mark above it; `push` and `grow` use the
20	derived `issue` of Part XIV (`Arena.IssueD`: its static checks, the availability `fail`, then
21	`split` of `internal` and `store` of the block); `grow` is in place only (same base, extension into
22	the space directly after the block, `fail` otherwise). DS2-1: `mark` requires the administrative
23	right of §36 (`AdminRight`), else `reject`. DS2-2: `grow` stores the new block authority into the
24	place that currently holds the block authority `b`. DS2-3: a dead stack (`internal` inactive)
25	invalidates its marks, so `rewind` of a mark of a dead stack is `fail`, checked with the dead or
26	foreign mark, before the right. Also part of DS-v2: `push` without room is `fail`; `grow` of a `b`
27	that is no block of the stack is `reject`; §76.5 applies to `newStack`; the dead or foreign mark is
28	checked before the right of §36; §36 applies to `rewind`.
29	
30	Every `ok` step of the library is a sequence of kernel steps O1–O16 (`DReach.reachable`), so the
31	abstraction adds no rights to the kernel (§36).
32	-/
33	
34	namespace Ern.Lib.DataStack
35	
36	open Ern.MemoryModel Ern.MemoryModel.Access Ern.MemoryModel.Arena
37	
38	/-! ## Library state (DS-v2; §38, §46, §47) -/
39	
40	/-- A block issued by a stack (DS-v2, non-normative; recorded like the issuances of §46): position
41	`base` of its first cell and number `size` of cells among the ordered cells of the stack, block
42	authority `auth`, destination `dst` that received it (at `push`, or at the `grow` that issued it,
43	DS2-2). -/
44	structure Blk where
45	  base : Nat
46	  size : Nat
47	  auth : Nat
48	  dst : Nat
49	deriving DecidableEq, Repr
50	
51	/-- A mark (DS-v2, non-normative: "marks carry stack identity and a fresh mark identifier";
52	library metadata of an administrative abstraction, §36, §38): the identity of its stack, its fresh
53	identifier, the top of the stack when it was taken. -/
54	structure Mark where
55	  stack : Nat
56	  id : Nat
57	  top : Nat
58	deriving DecidableEq, Repr
59	
60	/-- A stack (DS-v2, non-normative; library state, §38, §46): administered storage, `internal`
61	authority held by the stack value (§36), ordered cells (the leaves of the storage at creation),
62	top (the cells at positions `≥ top` are available), issued blocks (oldest first), and the ordered
63	list of live marks (DS-v2: "the stack keeps the ordered list of live marks"). -/
64	structure Stack where
65	  storage : Nat
66	  internal : Nat
67	  cells : List Nat
68	  top : Nat
69	  blocks : List Blk
70	  marks : List Mark
71	deriving DecidableEq, Repr
72	
73	/-- State of the stack library (DS-v2, non-normative; §38: administrative states of library
74	abstractions are separate from `S₃`): the kernel state, the stack registry (a stack is identified
75	by its index; stacks are never removed) and the next fresh mark identifier. -/
76	structure DState where
77	  kern : S3
78	  stacks : List Stack
79	  fresh : Nat
80	
81	/-- Initial state (§47: the kernel's initial state; the library registry starts empty; DS-v2,
82	non-normative: no mark identifier given out). -/
83	def DState.init (statics : Statics) : DState := ⟨S3.init statics, [], 0⟩
84	
85	/-- The `n` cells from position `b` of the stack, leaves of the administered storage (§46; DS-v2,
86	non-normative). -/
87	def cellsOf (st : Stack) (b n : Nat) : List Nat := (st.cells.drop b).take n
88	
89	/-- The cells above mark `m` (DS-v2, non-normative, "a cell above m"; reading DS-R1; §46
90	available leaves): the positions from the top of `m` to the current top, those that `rewind m`
91	returns to available. -/
92	def above (st : Stack) (m : Mark) : List Nat := cellsOf st m.top (st.top - m.top)
93	
94	/-- The stack seen as an administration entry (§46, §36; DS-v2, non-normative): storage,
95	`internal`, available cells (positions `≥ top`) and issued blocks. Used for `MetaRight` and the
96	static checks of the derived `issue`, which read only the storage and `internal`. -/
97	def Stack.entry (st : Stack) : ArenaEntry :=
98	  ⟨st.storage, st.internal, st.cells.drop st.top,
99	    st.blocks.map fun x => (cellsOf st x.base x.size, x.auth)⟩
100	
101	/-- The block of the stack whose authority is `b` (§46 issuances; DS-v2, non-normative). -/
102	def Stack.block (st : Stack) (b : Nat) : Option Blk := st.blocks.find? fun y => decide (y.auth = b)
103	
104	/-- A live mark of stack `j` (DS-v2, non-normative: a mark that is neither dead nor foreign; it
105	decides the `fail` case of `rewind`, §58): the stack is live (`internal` is active, §46 read for a
106	stack; DS2-3: a dead stack invalidates its marks), the mark names stack `j` and it belongs to the
107	list of live marks of the stack. -/
108	def LiveMark (s : S3) (j : Nat) (st : Stack) (m : Mark) : Prop :=
109	  s.Active st.internal ∧ m.stack = j ∧ m ∈ st.marks
110	
111	/-- Decidability of `LiveMark` (§58; DS-v2). -/
112	instance (s : S3) (j : Nat) (st : Stack) (m : Mark) : Decidable (LiveMark s j st m) := by
113	  unfold LiveMark; infer_instance
114	
115	/-- The administrative right of §36 for a stack (DS-v2, non-normative, with §36 and §46 read for a
116	stack): the stack is live (`internal` is active) and `MetaRight`, `Modify` exercisable on the stack
117	value, the place holding `internal`. -/
118	def AdminRight (s : S3) (st : Stack) : Prop := s.Active st.internal ∧ MetaRight s st.entry
119	
120	/-- Decidability of `AdminRight` (§36; DS-v2). -/
121	instance (s : S3) (st : Stack) : Decidable (AdminRight s st) := by
122	  unfold AdminRight; infer_instance
123	
124	/-! ## `newStack` and the guard of §56 -/
125	
126	/-- The stack registry as a registry of live administrations (§56; DS-v2, non-normative): the
127	`internal` identities of its live stacks. -/
128	def stackInternals (s : S3) (stacks : List Stack) : List Nat :=
129	  (stacks.filter fun st => decide (s.Active st.internal)).map (·.internal)
130	
131	/-- Preconditions of `newStack(storage, internal)` (DS-v2, non-normative; §56): those of `newArena`
132	other than its guard (`NewArenaBase`, §76.1–§76.3, §76.5 and §76.6 read for a stack), and the guard
133	of §56 over the stack registry and every other registry of live administrations `others`. -/
134	structure NewStackPre (s : S3) (stacks : List Stack) (others : List (List Nat))
135	    (storage internal : Nat) : Prop where
136	  /-- §76.1–§76.3, §76.5, §76.6, read for a stack (DS-v2). -/
137	  base : NewArenaBase s storage internal
138	  /-- §56: no live administration of any registry uses `internal`. -/
139	  guard : Guard56 (stackInternals s stacks :: others) internal
140	
141	/-- Decidability of `NewStackPre` (§56; DS-v2). -/
142	instance (s : S3) (stacks : List Stack) (others : List (List Nat)) (storage internal : Nat) :
143	    Decidable (NewStackPre s stacks others storage internal) :=
144	  decidable_of_iff (NewArenaBase s storage internal ∧
145	    Guard56 (stackInternals s stacks :: others) internal)
146	    ⟨fun ⟨a, b⟩ => ⟨a, b⟩, fun ⟨a, b⟩ => ⟨a, b⟩⟩
147	
148	/-- Effect of `newStack` (DS-v2, non-normative; §36: registration adds no rights): a stack whose
149	cells are the leaves of the storage, top 0, no block, no mark; the kernel state is unchanged. -/
150	def newStackEff (D : DState) (storage internal : Nat) : DState :=
151	  { D with stacks := D.stacks ++ [⟨storage, internal, footprint D.kern.P storage, 0, [], []⟩] }
152	
153	/-- `newStack` as a relation (DS-v2, non-normative; §56, §58): `ok` or `reject`. -/
154	def NewStackStep (others : List (List Nat)) (storage internal : Nat) (D : DState) :
155	    Outcome3 DState → Prop :=
156	  Guarded (NewStackPre D.kern D.stacks others storage internal) (newStackEff D storage internal)
157	
158	/-! ## `push` (DS-v2: the derived `issue`, Part XIV, §77) -/
159	
160	/-- Metadata after `push` (DS-v2, non-normative; as the `ok` effect of §77 on §46 metadata): the
161	cells leave the available part (the top rises by `size`), the block is recorded. -/
162	def pushMeta (st : Stack) (size a dst : Nat) : Stack :=
163	  { st with top := st.top + size, blocks := st.blocks ++ [⟨st.top, size, a, dst⟩] }
164	
165	/-- `push(j, size, dst)` (DS-v2, non-normative: "push uses the derived issue"): the derived `issue`
166	of Part XIV (`Arena.IssueD`) of the `size` cells at the top into `dst`, on the stack seen as an
167	entry: its static checks (`IssueStatic`, §77.1, §77.2, with `MetaRight` of §36), then `fail`, the
168	state unchanged, when fewer than `size` cells are left (availability, §77.4; DS-v2, Q11 (a)),
169	then `split` of `internal` on the cells (O2) and `store` of the block, of fresh identity `|A|`, into
170	`dst` (O8). -/
171	inductive PushStep (k : K) (j size dst : Nat) (D : DState) : Outcome3 DState → Prop where
172	  | noStack : D.stacks[j]? = none → PushStep k j size dst D .reject
173	  | static {st : Stack} : D.stacks[j]? = some st →
174	      ¬ IssueStatic D.kern st.entry (cellsOf st st.top size) dst → PushStep k j size dst D .reject
175	  | fail {st : Stack} : D.stacks[j]? = some st →
176	      IssueStatic D.kern st.entry (cellsOf st st.top size) dst →
177	      ¬ st.top + size ≤ st.cells.length → PushStep k j size dst D .fail
178	  | split {st : Stack} : D.stacks[j]? = some st →
179	      IssueStatic D.kern st.entry (cellsOf st st.top size) dst →
180	      st.top + size ≤ st.cells.length →
181	      SplitStep k st.internal [cellsOf st st.top size] D.kern .reject →
182	      PushStep k j size dst D .reject
183	  | store {st : Stack} {s₁ : S3} : D.stacks[j]? = some st →
184	      IssueStatic D.kern st.entry (cellsOf st st.top size) dst →
185	      st.top + size ≤ st.cells.length →
186	      SplitStep k st.internal [cellsOf st st.top size] D.kern (.ok s₁) →
187	      StoreStep D.kern.A.length dst s₁ .reject → PushStep k j size dst D .reject
188	  | ok {st : Stack} {s₁ s₂ : S3} : D.stacks[j]? = some st →
189	      IssueStatic D.kern st.entry (cellsOf st st.top size) dst →
190	      st.top + size ≤ st.cells.length →
191	      SplitStep k st.internal [cellsOf st st.top size] D.kern (.ok s₁) →
192	      StoreStep D.kern.A.length dst s₁ (.ok s₂) →
193	      PushStep k j size dst D
194	        (.ok ⟨s₂, D.stacks.set j (pushMeta st size D.kern.A.length dst), D.fresh⟩)
195	
196	/-! ## `mark` (DS-v2) -/
197	
198	/-- Metadata after `mark` (DS-v2, non-normative; library metadata, §36, §38): a mark naming stack
199	`j`, with the fresh identifier `fresh` and the current top, is appended to the live marks. -/
200	def markMeta (j : Nat) (st : Stack) (fresh : Nat) : Stack :=
201	  { st with marks := st.marks ++ [⟨j, fresh, st.top⟩] }
202	
203	/-- `mark(j)` (DS-v2, non-normative; §58 outcomes): `reject` on a missing stack; `reject` without
204	the administrative right of §36 (DS2-1); otherwise `ok`, metadata only (no right created, §36), the
205	identifier is fresh. -/
206	inductive MarkStep (j : Nat) (D : DState) : Outcome3 DState → Prop where
207	  | noStack : D.stacks[j]? = none → MarkStep j D .reject
208	  | static {st : Stack} : D.stacks[j]? = some st → ¬ AdminRight D.kern st → MarkStep j D .reject
209	  | ok {st : Stack} : D.stacks[j]? = some st → AdminRight D.kern st →
210	      MarkStep j D (.ok ⟨D.kern, D.stacks.set j (markMeta j st D.fresh), D.fresh + 1⟩)
211	
212	/-- `mark_rejects_without_right` (DS-v2, non-normative, DS2-1: `mark` requires `AdminRight` on the
213	stack, else `reject`; §36, §58): on an existing stack without the administrative right of §36,
214	`mark` has the outcome `reject` and no other. -/
215	theorem mark_rejects_without_right {j : Nat} {D : DState} {st : Stack}
216	    (hst : D.stacks[j]? = some st) (ha : ¬ AdminRight D.kern st) :
217	    MarkStep j D .reject ∧ ∀ o, MarkStep j D o → o = .reject := by
218	  refine ⟨.static hst ha, fun o ho => ?_⟩
219	  cases ho with
220	  | noStack => rfl
221	  | static => rfl
222	  | ok h ha' => rw [hst] at h; cases h; exact absurd ha' ha
223	
224	/-! ## `rewind` (DS-v2) -/
225	
226	/-- Metadata after `rewind m` (DS-v2, non-normative; as the `ok` effect of §78 on §46 metadata):
227	the cells above `m` return to available (the top returns to the top of `m`), the blocks from that
228	top are forgotten, `m` and every later mark are removed. -/
229	def rewindMeta (st : Stack) (m : Mark) : Stack :=
230	  { st with
231	    top := m.top
232	    blocks := st.blocks.filter fun x => decide (x.base < m.top)
233	    marks := st.marks.takeWhile fun x => decide (x ≠ m) }
234	
235	/-- `rewind(j, m)` (DS-v2, non-normative): `reject` on a missing stack; `fail`, the state
236	unchanged, on a dead or foreign mark, a mark of a dead stack included (DS2-3), before the right;
237	`reject` without the administrative right of §36; then the derived `reset` of Part XIV on the cells
238	above `m`: `split` of `internal` on them (O2), which rejects when an active authority derived from
239	`internal` covers one of them (`rewind_rejects_live_above`), and `release` of the derived authority
240	(O3); `ok`: the cells return to available, `m` and the later marks are removed. -/
241	inductive RewindStep (k : K) (j : Nat) (m : Mark) (D : DState) : Outcome3 DState → Prop where
242	  | noStack : D.stacks[j]? = none → RewindStep k j m D .reject
243	  | dead {st : Stack} : D.stacks[j]? = some st → ¬ LiveMark D.kern j st m →
244	      RewindStep k j m D .fail
245	  | static {st : Stack} : D.stacks[j]? = some st → LiveMark D.kern j st m →
246	      ¬ AdminRight D.kern st → RewindStep k j m D .reject

315	/-! ## `grow` (DS-v2: in place, the derived `issue`) -/

317	/-- In-place extension (DS-v2, non-normative: "extension into the space directly after the
318	block"; the availability check of the derived `issue`, §77.4): the block ends at the top, and
319	`extra` available cells follow it. -/
320	def InPlace (st : Stack) (x : Blk) (extra : Nat) : Prop :=
321	  x.base + x.size = st.top ∧ st.top + extra ≤ st.cells.length
322	
323	/-- Decidability of `InPlace` (§77.4; DS-v2). -/
324	instance (st : Stack) (x : Blk) (extra : Nat) : Decidable (InPlace st x extra) := by

329	def growBlk (x : Blk) (extra a d : Nat) : Blk := ⟨x.base, x.size + extra, a, d⟩

332	top rises by `extra`; the block is replaced by the grown block. -/
333	def growMeta (st : Stack) (x : Blk) (extra a d : Nat) : Stack :=
334	  { st with
335	    top := st.top + extra
336	    blocks := st.blocks.map fun y => if y.auth = x.auth then growBlk x extra a d else y }

339	DS2-2: the destination of `grow` is the place that currently holds the block authority). -/
340	def holderPlace (s : S3) (a : Nat) : Option Nat :=
341	  match s.A[a]? with
342	  | some y => match y.holder with
343	    | .place v => some v
344	    | .frame _ => none

347	/-- `grow(j, b, extra)` (DS-v2, non-normative: in place only, using the derived `issue`): `reject`

349	`issue` of Part XIV (`Arena.IssueD`) of the region of the same base and of size `size + extra` into
350	the place `d` that holds `b` when `grow` starts (DS2-2), on the released state: `reject` when no
351	place holds `b` (there is no destination, §77.2; never on library-reachable states,
352	`DReach.grow_holder`), its static checks (`IssueStatic`, §77.1, §77.2), `fail`, the state
353	unchanged, unless the extension is in place (DS-v1 "fail otherwise", availability §77.4), `split`
354	of `internal` (O2) and `store` of the new block into `d` (O8). -/
355	inductive GrowStep (k : K) (j b extra : Nat) (D : DState) : Outcome3 DState → Prop where
356	  | noStack : D.stacks[j]? = none → GrowStep k j b extra D .reject

364	      0 < extra → ReleaseStep b D.kern (.ok s₁) → holderPlace D.kern b = none →
365	      GrowStep k j b extra D .reject
366	  | static {st : Stack} {x : Blk} {s₁ : S3} {d : Nat} : D.stacks[j]? = some st →
367	      st.block b = some x → 0 < extra → ReleaseStep b D.kern (.ok s₁) →
368	      holderPlace D.kern b = some d →
369	      ¬ IssueStatic s₁ st.entry (cellsOf st x.base (x.size + extra)) d →
370	      GrowStep k j b extra D .reject
371	  | fail {st : Stack} {x : Blk} {s₁ : S3} {d : Nat} : D.stacks[j]? = some st →
372	      st.block b = some x → 0 < extra → ReleaseStep b D.kern (.ok s₁) →
373	      holderPlace D.kern b = some d →
374	      IssueStatic s₁ st.entry (cellsOf st x.base (x.size + extra)) d →

378	      holderPlace D.kern b = some d →
379	      IssueStatic s₁ st.entry (cellsOf st x.base (x.size + extra)) d → InPlace st x extra →
380	      SplitStep k st.internal [cellsOf st x.base (x.size + extra)] s₁ .reject →
381	      GrowStep k j b extra D .reject

383	      st.block b = some x → 0 < extra → ReleaseStep b D.kern (.ok s₁) →

386	      SplitStep k st.internal [cellsOf st x.base (x.size + extra)] s₁ (.ok s₂) →

397	/-! ## Library runs (DS-v2; §36, §56, §57) -/
398	
399	/-- One `ok` step of the stack library (DS-v2, non-normative): a kernel step O1–O16 of
400	non-administrative code, the registry unchanged; `newStack` with the guard of §56 against the other
401	registries `others`; `push`, `mark`, `rewind`, `grow`. -/
402	inductive DStep (k : K) : DState → DState → Prop where
403	  | kernel {D : DState} {s' : S3} : KStep k D.kern s' → DStep k D ⟨s', D.stacks, D.fresh⟩
404	  | newStack {D D' : DState} {others : List (List Nat)} {storage i : Nat} :
405	      NewStackStep others storage i D (.ok D') → DStep k D D'
406	  | push {D D' : DState} {j size dst : Nat} : PushStep k j size dst D (.ok D') → DStep k D D'
407	  | mark {D D' : DState} {j : Nat} : MarkStep j D (.ok D') → DStep k D D'
408	  | rewind {D D' : DState} {j : Nat} {m : Mark} : RewindStep k j m D (.ok D') → DStep k D D'
409	  | grow {D D' : DState} {j b extra : Nat} : GrowStep k j b extra D (.ok D') → DStep k D D'

411	/-- States reachable from the initial state by library steps (DS-v2, non-normative; §47). -/
412	inductive DReach (k : K) (statics : Statics) : DState → Prop where
413	  | init : DReach k statics (DState.init statics)
414	  | step {D D' : DState} : DReach k statics D → DStep k D D' → DReach k statics D'
415	
416	/-- Finite sequences of library steps (DS-v2, non-normative; §58 `ok` transitions). -/
417	inductive DRun (k : K) : DState → DState → Prop where
418	  | refl (D : DState) : DRun k D D
419	  | tail {D D' D'' : DState} : DRun k D D' → DStep k D' D'' → DRun k D D''
420	
421	/-- The kernel part of a library step is reached by kernel steps (§36: the abstraction adds no
422	rights to the kernel; Part XIV: `issue` is `split` then `store`, the reset part of `rewind` is
423	`split` then `release`; DS-v2). -/
424	theorem DStep.reachable {k : K} {statics : Statics} {D D' : DState}
425	    (hr : Reachable k statics D.kern) (h : DStep k D D') : Reachable k statics D'.kern := by
426	  cases h with
427	  | kernel hk => exact .step hr hk
428	  | newStack hs => obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 hs; exact hr
429	  | push hs =>
430	    cases hs with
431	    | ok _ _ _ hsp hst => exact .step (.step hr (.split hsp)) (.store hst)
432	  | mark hs => cases hs with | ok _ _ => exact hr
433	  | rewind hs =>
434	    cases hs with
435	    | ok _ _ _ hsp hrl => exact .step (.step hr (.split hsp)) (.release hrl)
436	  | grow hs =>
437	    cases hs with
438	    | ok _ _ _ hrl _ _ _ hsp hst =>
439	      exact .step (.step (.step hr (.release hrl)) (.split hsp)) (.store hst)

441	/-- The kernel state of every library-reachable state is kernel-reachable (§36, §57; DS-v2). -/
442	theorem DReach.reachable {k : K} {statics : Statics} {D : DState} (h : DReach k statics D) :
443	    Reachable k statics D.kern := by
444	  induction h with
445	  | init => exact .init
446	  | step _ hs ih => exact hs.reachable ih

451	theorem getElem?_set_cases {α : Type} {l : List α} {j i : Nat} {v x : α}
452	    (h : (l.set j v)[i]? = some x) : (i = j ∧ x = v) ∨ (i ≠ j ∧ l[i]? = some x) := by
453	  rw [List.getElem?_set] at h
454	  by_cases hij : j = i
455	  · subst hij; simp only [↓reduceIte] at h; split at h
456	    · cases h; exact .inl ⟨rfl, rfl⟩
457	    · cases h
458	  · simp only [hij, ↓reduceIte] at h; exact .inr ⟨Ne.symm hij, h⟩

462	theorem getElem?_append_single {α : Type} {l : List α} {x y : α} {i : Nat}
463	    (h : (l ++ [x])[i]? = some y) : l[i]? = some y ∨ y = x := by
464	  rw [List.getElem?_append] at h
465	  split at h
466	  · exact .inl h
467	  · cases hc : i - l.length with
468	    | zero => rw [hc] at h; simp at h; exact .inr h.symm
469	    | succ n => rw [hc] at h; simp at h

474	    (pre ++ m :: post).takeWhile (fun x => decide (x ≠ m)) = pre
475	  | [], post, _ => by simp
476	  | a :: pre, post, h => by
477	    have ha : a ≠ m := fun e => h (e ▸ List.mem_cons_self ..)
478	    have ih := takeWhile_ne_append (pre := pre) post (fun h' => h (List.mem_cons_of_mem _ h'))

480	    simp only [ha, ne_eq, not_false_eq_true, decide_true, ↓reduceIte, ih]

484	theorem take_prefix_take_add {α : Type} : ∀ (l : List α) (n e : Nat), l.take n <+: l.take (n + e)

516	/-- `rewind_rejects_live_above` (DS-v2, non-normative: "rewind m … rejects if an active authority
517	derived from internal covers a cell above m"): for a live mark `m` of an existing stack (its stack
518	live, DS2-3), if an active authority derived from `internal` covers a cell above `m`, `rewind m`
519	has the outcome `reject` and no other: either the administrative right of §36 fails, or `split` of
520	`internal` on the cells above `m` is rejected, since `internal` no longer has effective `Modify` on
521	that cell (§43, §61.1). -/
522	theorem rewind_rejects_live_above {k : K} {D : DState} {j : Nat} {st : Stack} {m : Mark}
523	    (hst : D.stacks[j]? = some st) (hm : LiveMark D.kern j st m) {x l : Nat} {y : Authority}
524	    (hy : D.kern.A[x]? = some y) (ya : y.active = true) (hx : st.internal ∈ D.kern.ancs x)
525	    (hly : l ∈ y.footprint) (hl : l ∈ above st m) :
526	    RewindStep k j m D .reject ∧ ∀ o, RewindStep k j m D o → o = .reject := by
527	  have hn : ¬ SplitPre k D.kern st.internal [above st m] := fun h =>
528	    no_desc_of_modify hy ya hly hx (h.modifyOn _ (List.mem_singleton_self _) l hl)
529	  refine ⟨?_, fun o ho => ?_⟩
530	  · by_cases ha : AdminRight D.kern st
531	    · exact .split hst hm ha (.reject hn)
532	    · exact .static hst hm ha
533	  · cases ho with
534	    | noStack => rfl
535	    | dead h hd => rw [hst] at h; cases h; exact absurd hm hd
536	    | static => rfl
537	    | split => rfl
538	    | release => rfl
539	    | ok h _ _ hsp =>
540	      rw [hst] at h; cases h
541	      exact absurd (Guarded.ok_iff.1 hsp).1 hn
